item.desc: init : Initialize a new Git repository in current directory
item.desc1: Creates a hidden .git directory containing all metadata, object database, and head references required for version control.
item.desc2: Run once when starting a new local project from scratch before adding files.
item.alt: git init --bare (for central bare repository without working directory)

item.desc: config : Set your global username for all commits
item.desc1: Writes user.name to global ~/.gitconfig file. Author name attached to all future commits across repositories.
item.desc2: Essential one-time setup on new machines so your commit author details are correctly identified on GitHub/GitLab.
item.alt: git config user.name "Name" (set local repo author name only)

item.desc: config : Set your global email for all commits
item.desc1: Writes user.email to global ~/.gitconfig file. Links commits to your GitHub/GitLab account profile.
item.desc2: Set your GitHub account email address so commits map correctly to your GitHub user profile and contribution graph.
item.alt: git config user.email "email" (set local repo email only)

item.desc: config : Set default text editor for Git (e.g., code --wait, vim, nano)
item.desc1: Configures the text editor executable invoked by Git when writing commit messages or resolving interactive rebases.
item.desc2: Use "code --wait" for VS Code or "notepad++" for Notepad++ so Git pauses execution until you save and close the editor window.

item.desc: config : Display all current Git configuration settings
item.desc1: Reads combined configuration values from system, global, and local .git/config files.
item.desc2: Use when troubleshooting Git setup, verifying username/email, or checking remote alias configurations.

item.desc: clone : Clone a remote repository to your local machine
item.desc1: Copies full remote repository history, sets up remote origin tracking branch, and checks out default branch to working directory.
item.desc2: Use when onboarding to an existing project on GitHub to download full project code and commit history locally.
item.alt: git clone --depth 1 <repourl> (shallow clone latest commit only)
item.warning: Downloads entire commit history; check available disk space

item.desc: remote : Connect local repository to remote GitHub repository
item.desc1: Registers remote URL short-name alias ('origin') in .git/config pointing to your remote server repository.
item.desc2: Run after `git init` when creating a brand new project locally and linking it to a newly created GitHub repository.
item.alt: git remote add upstream <repourl> (add parent repo link for forks)
item.warning: Will raise an error if remote alias 'origin' already exists

item.desc: remote : List all configured remote repositories with URLs
item.desc1: Lists all remote short-name aliases (like origin, upstream) alongside fetch and push target URLs.
item.desc2: Use to verify whether local repo is connected to the correct GitHub URL or fork remote.

item.desc: remote : Remove a remote repository connection
item.desc1: Deletes the 'origin' remote reference from .git/config. Does not delete remote files on GitHub.
item.desc2: Use when changing remote repository URLs or replacing an incorrect origin link.
item.warning: Deletes remote reference link locally; does not touch remote server

item.desc: remote : Clean up stale local tracking references for deleted remote branches
item.desc1: Removes local references to origin/branch names that have already been deleted on the remote server.
item.desc2: Run periodically or after PRs are merged and deleted on GitHub to keep your `git branch -a` listing clean.
item.alt: git fetch --prune (fetch and prune stale branches in one step)
item.warning: Removes local tracking branches whose remote counterparts no longer exist

item.desc: status : Show current repository status (modified/staged/untracked files)
item.desc1: Compares Working Directory against Staging Index and HEAD commit. Highlights modified, untracked, and staged files.
item.desc2: Your primary compass command! Run frequently to verify file state before committing or switching branches.

item.tagq: status, check, info, state, compact, short
item.desc: status : Show compact repository status with symbols (?? = untracked, M = modified)
item.desc1: Displays two-letter status codes per file (Column 1 = Staging status, Column 2 = Working directory status).
item.desc2: Ideal for quick inspection when working with dozens of changed files in large projects.

item.desc: diff : Show unstaged changes in working directory
item.desc1: Compares modifications in Working Directory against the Staging Area (Index). Shows exact line modifications.
item.desc2: Review changes before running `git add` to double-check line edits and avoid accidental commits.
item.alt: git diff --staged (show changes already staged for commit)

item.desc: diff : Show changes that are staged for commit
item.desc1: Compares Staging Area (Index) against HEAD commit. Displays code changes that will be included in next commit.
item.desc2: Run immediately before `git commit` as a final sanity check of what will be recorded in history.

item.desc: diff : Compare current working directory against the previous commit (HEAD~1)
item.desc1: Compares Working Directory and Index combined directly against parent commit snapshot.
item.desc2: Useful when reviewing total changes introduced across the last commit and your uncommitted work combined.

item.desc: diff : Show differences between two branches (e.g., main..develop)
item.desc1: Calculates line-by-line differences between tips of two specified branches.
item.desc2: Compare feature branch against main branch before creating a Pull Request or performing a merge.
item.alt: git diff <branch1>...<branch2> (shows changes since common ancestor)

item.desc: add : Stage all modified and new files in current directory
item.desc1: Copies all new and modified files from Working Directory into the Staging Index.
item.desc2: Use when you are ready to prepare all recent file edits in current folder for the next commit snapshot.
item.alt: git add -A (stage all changes across entire repository tree)
item.warning: Be careful not to stage unwanted build artifacts or secret config files

item.desc: add : Stage a specific file for commit (e.g., git add index.html)
item.desc1: Selectively copies target file into Staging Index, leaving other modified files unstaged.
item.desc2: Use when creating granular, topic-focused commits containing only relevant file changes.

item.desc: add : Stage changes interactively (hunk by hunk) - great for splitting commits
item.desc1: Opens interactive prompt asking per-hunk [y,n,q,a,d,s,e] to stage partial code changes inside a single file.
item.desc2: Perfect for splitting multiple unrelated feature edits in one file into separate clean commits.

item.desc: commit : Commit staged changes with a custom message
item.desc1: Creates immutable commit object in .git database containing tree snapshot, author info, timestamp, and message.
item.desc2: Primary action to record project history milestone. Write clear present-tense commit messages.
item.alt: git commit -am "<commitmsg>" (automatically stage tracked files and commit)
item.warning: Requires changes to be staged first via `git add`

item.desc: commit : Stage all tracked files AND commit with one command
item.desc1: Automatically stages modifications in already-tracked files, skipping untracked files, then records commit.
item.desc2: Fast shortcut when editing existing files in smaller projects without creating new untracked files.
item.warning: Does NOT stage brand new untracked files!

item.tagq: commit, amend, fix, edit, update, last
item.desc: commit : Replace the last commit with a new one (different message)
item.desc1: Rewrites the tip of current branch, creating a replacement commit object with updated message/staged content.
item.desc2: Fix typos in your latest commit message or add forgotten staged files before pushing to remote.
item.warning: DANGER: Do NOT use if commit has already been pushed to public remote branch!

item.tagq: commit, amend, fix, edit, update, last, keep
item.desc: commit : Combine staged changes into last commit without changing message
item.desc1: Absorbs staged changes into the most recent commit without modifying commit message title.
item.desc2: Ideal when you forgot a small file tweak in your last commit and want to include it without creating clutter.
item.warning: DANGER: Rewrites local commit history; avoid if already pushed!

item.desc: commit : Create a fixup commit target for automatic squashing during rebase
item.desc1: Generates a commit with message prefixed `fixup! <hash>`. Works seamlessly with `git rebase -i --autosquash`.
item.desc2: Best practice when fixing bugs in older un-pushed commits while keeping git log organized.
item.alt: git commit --squash <commithash> (merge content and combine log messages)
item.warning: Requires interactive rebase with --autosquash to consolidate

item.desc: branch : List all local branches (* indicates current branch)
item.desc1: Reads local references in .git/refs/heads/. Highlights active branch with asterisk.
item.desc2: Check which branch you are currently working on before starting new work.
item.alt: git branch -a (list all local and remote branches)

item.desc: branch : List all local and remote branches
item.desc1: Displays local branches alongside remote-tracking branch references (.git/refs/remotes/origin/).
item.desc2: Use to view available remote feature branches created by teammates on GitHub.

item.desc: branch : List branches that have already been merged into current HEAD
item.desc1: Filters branch list to show only branches whose commits are reachable from current HEAD.
item.desc2: Identify stale feature branches that can safely be deleted with `git branch -d`.

item.desc: branch : Create a new branch (but don't switch to it)
item.desc1: Creates a new pointer reference pointing to current HEAD commit snapshot.
item.desc2: Creates a new isolated development path without changing working directory.
item.warning: Does not automatically switch working directory to new branch

item.desc: checkout : Switch to an existing branch
item.desc1: Updates HEAD reference pointer and restores Working Directory files to match target branch commit.
item.desc2: Switch context to work on a feature branch, hotfix, or main line.
item.alt: git switch <branchname> (newer, clearer Git command syntax)
item.warning: Stash or commit uncommitted changes before switching to prevent conflicts

item.desc: checkout : Create and switch to a new branch in one command
item.desc1: Combines branch creation pointer with immediate HEAD update and working directory switch.
item.desc2: Standard workflow command when starting work on a new feature or task.
item.warning: Ensure current branch is clean before switching

item.desc: switch : Switch to an existing branch (newer Git syntax)
item.desc1: Dedicated replacement command for switching branches (avoids confusion with file restore).
item.desc2: Recommended modern syntax for moving between branches.
item.warning: Commit or stash pending changes before switching

item.desc: switch : Create and switch to new branch (newer Git syntax)
item.desc1: Modern syntax dedicated to creating (-c = create) and checking out new branch.
item.desc2: Use when beginning work on a new feature ticket.

item.desc: branch : Delete a branch (safe - only if merged)
item.desc1: Deletes pointer reference in .git/refs/heads/ if branch changes have been fully merged into HEAD.
item.desc2: Clean up local feature branches after PR merge.
item.warning: Will fail with a warning if branch contains unmerged commits

item.desc: branch : Force delete a branch (even if not merged)
item.desc1: Deletes branch reference unconditionally, regardless of merge status.
item.desc2: Use when abandoning an experimental feature branch that you no longer need.
item.warning: WARNING: Commits exclusive to this branch will become unreferenced and lost!

item.desc: branch : Rename current branch to a new name
item.desc1: Renames branch reference pointer in .git/refs/heads/ to target name.
item.desc2: Fix typo in current branch name or adjust naming convention before pushing.
item.warning: If already pushed to remote, remote branch must be deleted and re-pushed

item.desc: merge : Merge changes from another branch into current branch
item.desc1: Integrates commit history of target branch into active branch, creating a merge commit if non-fast-forward.
item.desc2: Bring completed feature branch work back into main or develop branch.
item.alt: git merge --no-ff <branchname> (always generate merge commit node)
item.warning: May produce merge conflicts requiring manual text file editing

item.desc: merge : Cancel an in-progress merge and restore pre-merge state
item.desc1: Clears merge conflict markers and restores Working Directory and Index to pre-merge HEAD commit state.
item.desc2: Use when a merge produces overwhelming conflicts and you want to safely abort back to normal state.
item.warning: Only available while merge conflict state is active

item.desc: rebase : Reapply commits on top of another branch (cleaner history)
item.desc1: Rewinds current branch commits, updates base pointer to target branch tip, and reapplies commits sequentially.
item.desc2: Maintain linear, clean commit history without unnecessary merge commits before merging PR.
item.alt: git rebase -i HEAD~3 (interactive rebase to squash or edit commits)
item.warning: DANGER: Never rebase branches that have already been pushed and shared with teammates!

item.desc: rebase : Interactive rebase to squash, reorder, or edit last N commits
item.desc1: Launches text editor listing last N commits with commands: pick, reword, edit, squash, fixup, drop.
item.desc2: Clean up messy commit history, combine small fix commits ("squash"), or reword commit messages before pushing.
item.alt: git rebase -i <commithash> (rebase from specific commit hash base)
item.warning: DANGER: Only use on local, un-pushed commits!

item.desc: rebase : Transmit a branch topic onto a new base branch
item.desc1: Re-bases commits on current branch originating from branch2 onto branch1 base.
item.desc2: Used in complex multi-branch feature chains when a parent branch is changed or deleted.
item.warning: Advanced command; double check commit ranges

item.desc: rebase : Cancel an in-progress rebase and return to original branch state
item.desc1: Aborts rebase operation and restores branch reference pointer to state prior to rebase start.
item.desc2: Safely cancel out when encountering complex rebase conflicts.
item.warning: Only valid during active rebase state

item.desc: push : Push local commits to remote branch
item.desc1: Uploads local commit objects and updates target branch reference on remote server (origin).
item.desc2: Publish your local commits to GitHub so teammates can review code or pull changes.
item.alt: git push -u origin <branchname> (set upstream tracking on first push)
item.warning: Will be rejected if remote contains commits you don't have locally (run git pull first)

item.tagq: push, remote, upload, upstream, set, first
item.desc: push : Push and set upstream tracking for new branch (first push)
item.desc1: Pushes commits and links local branch to origin/branchname in .git/config for simple future `git push` calls.
item.desc2: Always use on your very first push of a newly created local branch.

item.tagq: push, force, override, update, remote, safe
item.desc: push : Force push (safe version) - only if remote hasn't changed
item.desc1: Overwrites remote history ONLY if no one else has pushed new commits to remote branch in the meantime.
item.desc2: Required after amending commits or running interactive rebase on your remote feature branch. Safer than `git push -f`.
item.alt: git push --force (dangerous force push without safety check)

item.desc: push : Delete a remote branch on GitHub
item.desc1: Sends remote delete reference command to origin to remove branch from remote server repository.
item.desc2: Clean up remote feature branch on GitHub after merging pull request.
item.warning: Deletes remote branch for all team members!

item.desc: pull : Fetch and merge remote changes into current branch
item.desc1: Executes `git fetch` followed immediately by `git merge origin/branchname` into active branch.
item.desc2: Sync local workspace with latest updates pushed by teammates on GitHub.
item.alt: git pull --rebase origin <branchname> (fetch and rebase instead of merge)
item.warning: May generate merge conflicts if local edits overlap remote commits

item.tagq: pull, rebase, fetch, sync, update, cleaner
item.desc: pull : Pull with rebase for cleaner linear history
item.desc1: Fetches remote commits and reapplies local un-pushed commits on top of incoming remote branch tip.
item.desc2: Preferred pull strategy in team environments to avoid cluttering history with small pull merge commits.
item.warning: May produce rebase conflict steps during re-application

item.desc: fetch : Download objects and refs from remote without merging
item.desc1: Downloads all new commits, branches, and tags from remote origin into local tracking refs (.git/refs/remotes/).
item.desc2: Safe inspection command! Download remote updates without touching your local working files.
item.alt: git fetch --all (fetch from all registered remotes)
item.next: git log HEAD..origin/main or git merge origin/main

item.desc: fetch : Fetch updates from all remote repositories
item.desc1: Downloads latest remote branches and commit histories across all configured remotes (origin, upstream, etc.).
item.desc2: Use when managing multiple remote repositories (e.g. fork and upstream main repository).

item.desc: restore : Discard local unstaged changes in specific file (newer Git)
item.desc1: Overwrites file in Working Directory with content snapshot from Index/HEAD commit.
item.desc2: Discard unwanted local edits in a file and reset it back to its last clean committed state.
item.warning: DANGER: Local unstaged edits in this file are permanently deleted!

item.desc: restore : Unstage a file from Staging Area (keep working directory edits)
item.desc1: Removes file from Staging Index, reverting index entry to match HEAD while keeping Working Directory changes intact.
item.desc2: Use when you accidentally staged a file with `git add` and want to remove it from staging before commit.
item.warning: Does not touch or delete edits in your working file

item.desc: restore : Interactively discard specific code changes (hunk by hunk)
item.desc1: Prompts hunk by hunk to selectively discard specific edits while keeping other changes in working file.
item.desc2: Discard temporary debug print statements while keeping actual code features.

item.desc: reset : Undo last commit but keep changes staged
item.desc1: Moves HEAD reference back 1 commit while leaving Staging Index and Working Directory untouched.
item.desc2: Use when you want to re-do the last commit with a different message or combine it with new additions.

item.desc: reset : Undo last commit but keep changes unstaged (default)
item.desc1: Moves HEAD reference back 1 commit and resets Staging Index, preserving edits in Working Directory.
item.desc2: Default reset mode. Use to break down a commit into smaller files and re-stage selectively.

item.desc: reset : UNDO last commit AND DELETE all changes - PERMANENT!
item.desc1: Moves HEAD back 1 commit AND resets both Index and Working Directory to match parent snapshot.
item.desc2: Use when discarding last commit and all associated file edits completely.
item.warning: DANGER: All uncommitted edits and changes from last commit are permanently destroyed!

item.desc: revert : Create new commit that undoes a previous commit (safe for public branches)
item.desc1: Inverts diff of target commit and generates a brand new forward commit recording the undo action.
item.desc2: Safe undo strategy for public/shared remote branches! Does not rewrite history timeline.
item.warning: Creates a new commit on active branch

item.desc: log : Show full commit history
item.desc1: Traverses commit object graph backwards from HEAD, displaying commit hashes, author, date, and full message body.
item.desc2: Browse detailed repository log history.

item.desc: log : Show compact commit history with short hashes
item.desc1: Outputs truncated 7-character commit hashes alongside commit title lines.
item.desc2: Quickly scan recent commit activity in terminal window.

item.desc: log : Display commit history with file modification statistics
item.desc1: Includes file insertion and deletion count summaries below each commit entry.
item.desc2: Inspect which files were affected across recent commits without viewing full diff code.
item.alt: git log -p (show full line diffs for each commit)

item.tagq: log, history, graph, tree, visual, branches
item.desc: log : Show commit history with ASCII branch graph visualization (last 15 commits)
item.desc1: Renders ASCII tree graph depicting branch splits, merges, tags, and HEAD references across all branches.
item.desc2: Best terminal command for understanding complex multi-branch project topologies!

item.desc: log : Search commit history for commits that added or removed specific code text
item.desc1: Uses Git "pickaxe" search to scan commit diff contents for additions or deletions of target code snippet.
item.desc2: Track down when a specific function, variable, or bug was introduced or removed from codebase.

item.desc: show : Show detailed information and code diff for a specific commit
item.desc1: Outputs full commit metadata plus line-by-line file diff associated with target commit hash.
item.desc2: Inspect exact code edits introduced in a specific commit hash.
item.alt: git show HEAD (view latest commit details)

item.desc: blame : Show who last modified each line of a file (e.g., git blame index.html)
item.desc1: Annotates each file line with author name, commit hash, and timestamp of last edit.
item.desc2: Identify who wrote a specific code snippet or when a line was last edited.

item.desc: log : Show commit history for a specific file (including file renames)
item.desc1: Traces file commit history past file rename boundaries to show complete file lifecycle.
item.desc2: Audit historical changes for a specific core file over time.

item.desc: stash : Save uncommitted changes to temporary stash (to switch branches cleanly)
item.desc1: Saves modified tracked files to internal stash stack reference (.git/refs/stash) and reverts working directory to HEAD.
item.desc2: Use when you must switch branches urgently without committing half-finished work.
item.alt: git stash save "<stashmsg>" (add descriptive label to stash)
item.warning: Removes modified changes from working files (saved safely in stash storage)
item.next: git checkout <branchname> or git stash pop

item.desc: stash : Save uncommitted changes with a descriptive message
item.desc1: Pushes working changes to stash stack labeled with custom description string for easy identification.
item.desc2: Best practice when maintaining multiple stashes simultaneously.
item.alt: git stash -u (include untracked files in stash)

item.desc: stash : List all stashed changes
item.desc1: Displays indexed stash entries: stash@{0}, stash@{1}, etc., with branch names and messages.
item.desc2: View all stashed work items currently saved in stash shelf.
item.alt: git stash show -p stash@{0} (view diff contents of stash entry)

item.desc: stash : Apply latest stash and remove it from stash list
item.desc1: Restores stashed file edits from top of stack (stash@{0}) into Working Directory and deletes stash entry.
item.desc2: Resume saved work after returning to your feature branch.
item.alt: git stash apply (apply stash without deleting from list)
item.warning: May produce conflict if working files have changed significantly

item.desc: stash : Apply latest stash but keep it in stash list
item.desc1: Applies stashed modifications to working directory while preserving stash@{0} entry in stash storage.
item.desc2: Useful when applying identical stashed changes across multiple branches.
item.alt: git stash apply stash@{1} (apply specific stash index)
item.warning: Stash item remains in stash list until dropped

item.desc: stash : Remove latest stash from stash list
item.desc1: Deletes targeted stash reference entry from stash stack.
item.desc2: Clean up stashes that are no longer needed.
item.alt: git stash drop stash@{1} (delete specific stash index)
item.warning: WARNING: Stash content is permanently deleted!

item.desc: stash : Create new branch from stash and apply stashed changes
item.desc1: Creates branch at commit where stash was made, applies stashed changes, and drops stash entry upon success.
item.desc2: Ideal when stashed changes conflict heavily with current branch updates.

item.desc: stash : Delete ALL stashes (cannot be undone!)
item.desc1: Empties entire stash stack database in .git/refs/stash.
item.desc2: Use during repository cleanup when all stashed work items are expired.
item.alt: git stash drop (delete single stash item)
item.warning: DANGER: ALL stashes are permanently deleted!

item.desc: tag : List all tags in the repository
item.desc1: Reads tags in .git/refs/tags/ sorted alphabetically.
item.desc2: View version release markers in project history.

item.desc: tag : Create an annotated tag (with message) for current commit
item.desc1: Creates full tag object in .git database with tagger name, date, message, and GPG signature support.
item.desc2: Mark production version release points (e.g. v1.0.0, v2.1.0).

item.desc: push : Push a specific tag to remote repository
item.desc1: Uploads tag object reference to remote server origin (triggers GitHub Release workflows).
item.desc2: Publish release tag to GitHub to trigger automated build/deploy CI pipelines.
item.alt: git push --tags (push all local tags at once)
item.warning: Tags are not pushed automatically with standard `git push`

item.desc: tag : Delete a local tag
item.desc1: Deletes local tag reference from .git/refs/tags/.
item.desc2: Remove mistyped local version tag.
item.warning: Deletes local tag only; does not remove tag on remote GitHub

item.desc: push : Delete a tag from remote repository
item.desc1: Sends remote command to origin to delete remote tag object reference.
item.desc2: Remove published release tag from GitHub server.
item.warning: Deletes remote release tag for all collaborators

item.desc: worktree : Create a separate working directory linked to active repository
item.desc1: Checks out target branch into a new filesystem directory while sharing central .git commit database.
item.desc2: Work on urgent hotfixes in parallel without stashing or switching current working directory!
item.alt: git worktree add -b <branchname> <repodir> (create new branch and worktree)
item.warning: Each worktree must checkout a different branch

item.desc: worktree : List all active linked worktree directories
item.desc1: Displays paths, commit hashes, and checked-out branch names for main and linked worktrees.
item.desc2: Inspect active parallel worktree folders registered with repository.
item.alt: git worktree prune (clean up stale worktree information)

item.desc: worktree : Remove a linked worktree directory
item.desc1: Deletes secondary worktree folder and unregisters administrative metadata from .git/worktrees/.
item.desc2: Clean up worktree directory after completing parallel hotfix task.
item.warning: Deletes files in target worktree folder; ensure uncommitted work is saved

item.desc: clean : Remove all untracked files and directories
item.desc1: Recursively deletes untracked files (-f) and directories (-d) from Working Directory.
item.desc2: Clean up build artifacts, temp files, and untracked code files.
item.alt: git clean -n (dry-run preview before actual deletion)
item.warning: DANGER: Permanently deletes untracked files! Cannot be undone!

item.desc: clean : Preview what files would be removed (dry-run)
item.desc1: Simulates clean action and lists untracked files without deleting anything.
item.desc2: ALWAYS run first before `git clean -fd` to avoid deleting important untracked files!
item.alt: git clean -nd (preview untracked directories as well)

item.desc: gc : Clean up unnecessary files and optimize repository database
item.desc1: Packs loose objects, compresses commit database, and prunes unreachable orphan objects.
item.desc2: Optimize repository performance and decrease .git folder size in mature projects.

item.desc: fsck : Verify integrity of Git repository database objects
item.desc1: Audits SHA-1 object database integrity and identifies dangling commits or corrupted objects.
item.desc2: Use when diagnosing repository corruption or locating lost dangling commits.

item.desc: submodule : Add an external repository as a submodule
item.desc1: Embeds external Git repository into a subdirectory and records commit pointer in .gitmodules file.
item.desc2: Include third-party libraries or shared component modules in your project.
item.alt: git submodule add <repourl> <filename> (custom target directory path)
item.warning: Tracks specific commit hash of sub-repository

item.desc: submodule : Initialize and update all submodules (including nested)
item.desc1: Clones missing submodule repositories and checks out commit hashes specified by main project.
item.desc2: Run immediately after cloning a fresh repository containing submodules.
item.alt: git submodule update --remote (pull latest submodule remote commits)

item.desc: cherry-pick : Apply specific commit from another branch to current branch
item.desc1: Copies diff of specified commit hash and applies it as a brand new commit on active branch.
item.desc2: Port a bug fix from develop branch to main release branch without merging full branch history.

item.desc: bisect : Start binary search to find commit that introduced a bug
item.desc1: Initiates binary search session across commit history range to quickly isolate bug origin commit.
item.desc2: Fastest method to find which commit broke a feature in large codebases!
item.alt: git bisect start <commithash> <commithash> (define bad and good endpoints)
item.warning: Temporarily checks out different historical commits
item.next: git bisect bad && git bisect good <commithash>

item.desc: bisect : Mark a commit as "good" (bug not present) during bisect
item.desc1: Informs bisect engine that current or specified commit hash works correctly, narrowing search range.
item.desc2: Step in bisect binary search debugging session.
item.alt: git bisect good (mark active HEAD as good)

item.desc: bisect : Mark a commit as "bad" (bug present) during bisect
item.desc1: Informs bisect engine that target commit contains bug, narrowing search range to earlier commits.
item.desc2: Step in bisect binary search debugging session.
item.alt: git bisect bad (mark active HEAD as bad)

item.desc: bisect : End bisect session and return to original branch
item.desc1: Terminates bisect search session and checks out original branch state prior to bisect start.
item.desc2: Always run after bisect finishes to return to normal development branch.

item.desc: reflog : Show history of all branch updates (recover lost commits)
item.desc1: Records every HEAD reference change (commits, checkouts, resets, rebases) in local repository.
item.desc2: LIFESAVER command! Use to recover accidentally deleted commits or lost branch references.

item.desc: archive : Export current repository commit snapshot as a ZIP file
item.desc1: Creates clean ZIP archive of active tree snapshot excluding .git folder metadata.
item.desc2: Export clean source code bundle for distribution or client release without git history.

item.desc: shortlog : Show commit count per contributor (sorted by number of commits)
item.desc1: Groups commit history by author name and displays total commit totals in descending order.
item.desc2: Summarize project contributor statistics.
